subject.title: San Lorenzo Unified School District — Measure J (Education Parcel Tax)

text: To renew expiring local school funding without increasing current tax rates; support academic excellence and programs in reading, writing, math, arts, science and technology; attract and retain highly qualified teachers and staff; and continue stable, local funding the State cannot take away; shall San Lorenzo Unified School District’s measure be adopted, renewing its expiring $99 parcel tax for 12 years, providing approximately $1.8 million annually, with senior exemptions, citizen oversight, and no funds for district administrators?

analysis.title: Impartial Analysis
analysis.by: Andrea L. Weddle, Interim County Counsel The above statement is an impartial analysis of Measure J, which is printed in full in this sample ballot pamphlet. text:
ANALYSIS BY THE COUNTY COUNSEL FOR THE COUNTY OF ALAMEDA OF A SAN LORENZO UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT SPECIAL PARCEL TAX MEASURE
Measure J (“Measure”), a San Lorenzo Unified School District (“District”) special parcel tax measure, seeks voter approval to renew the District’s expiring special parcel tax, beginning on July 1, 2027, maintaining the rate of $99 per parcel, for a period of twelve years.
The District estimates the parcel tax, if passed, will provide approximately $1,800,000 annually. The District will use the revenue only for the purposes listed in the Measure, which include, but are not limited to: supporting academic programs in reading, writing, math, arts, science and technology; preparing students for college and the workplace; and attracting and retaining highly qualified teachers and staff, including in high-need areas such as math, science, and special education. 
In addition to properties otherwise exempt from property taxes, the following people may apply to the District for exemptions on residential parcels owned and occupied as a principal residence: persons 65 years or older; persons receiving Supplemental Security Income for a disability; and persons receiving Social Security Disability Insurance Benefits who meet specified income requirements.
The Measure contains certain accountability provisions, including requiring the District to deposit parcel tax proceeds in a separate account, produce an annual report to the District’s governing board detailing the amount of funds collected and expended and the status of any projects funded by the proceeds, and conduct an annual financial audit by the District’s governing board to ensure parcel tax proceeds are spent for educational purposes. The District’s governing board will also appoint a citizen oversight committee to review the District’s use of parcel tax proceeds to ensure that they are expended for the purposes listed in the Measure. A school district has the authority to levy special taxes upon approval by two-thirds of the votes cast on the special tax proposal. (Cal. Const. art. XIII A, § 4; art. XIII C, § 2; Cal. Gov’t Code §§ 50075-50077, 50079, & 53722.) If two-thirds of the qualified electors voting on this Measure do not vote for approval, it will fail, and the District will not be authorized to levy the special parcel tax.
This Measure is placed on the ballot by the governing board of the District.

strong: Measure J will prevent cuts to the quality education in

text:
For nearly a decade, San Lorenzo Unified has relied on locally controlled funding to support academic programs, retain its excellent teaching staff, and prepare students for college and careers. That funding expires this year unless voters renew it.
Measure J won’t raise tax rates. It simply renews existing local funding at the current rate, continuing what voters have already approved.
Without Measure J, over $1,800,000 will need to be cut from the budget, forcing the layoff of 20 teachers, high staff turnover, and academic program reductions. Measure J keeps stable funding in place—

so San Lorenzo students continue to have access to qualified teachers and academic programs that prepare them for college and beyond. 
Even if you do not have school-age children, supporting quality education in local schools is a wise investment. Good schools improve the quality of life in our community and protect the value of our homes.
